output.summary: A bulbous ornamental herb of uncertain native origin, the garden tulip is widely cultivated in many countries. It is tall and late-blooming, usually bearing one large, showy flower above broad, spear-shaped leaves, while its bulb produces side bulbs.
output.edibilityNote: Bulbs may be eaten with little ill effect or dried, powdered and added to cereals or flour; flowers and bulbs can cause dermatitis.
